Theme 005 · Product UI as the stage

Light-Mode Data HUD

A near-white cockpit of sixteen hairline-ruled micro-panels — counters, sparklines, tickers — with terminal density and Swiss calm. A thin teal scanline sweeps the whole grid, the camera rack-focuses from panel to panel, and corner brackets snap onto the one number that is wrong.

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

All sixteen panels dim to ghost hairlines in a diagonal stagger (0.03 s each, top-left→bottom-right) as the plate grows from the checkout panel's position; the status ticker at the bottom scrolls left continuously and the Start free button lands on the final downbeat.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Tabular micro-panels — label + odometer number + sparkline, hairline-ruled.
  • Status ticker — top and bottom rails: LIVE, counts, anomalies.
  • Scanline sweep — 4 px teal line; panels brighten as it passes.
  • Corner brackets — focus device; ink for the hook, teal for Pulse, coral for the anomaly.
  • Hero panel — the one metric blown up with the deploy marker on the chart.
  • Calm decision card — a single white card with Roll back / Acknowledge.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Odometer digits — per-digit roll with steps(10) for 0.6 s, final value eases power4.out onto a downbeat.
  • Scanline sweep — crosses 960 px in 1.2 s linear, panels brighten +8 % with a 0.15 s delay as it passes; one sweep per 2 bars at 120 BPM.
  • Rack focus — non-hero panels blur 0→6 px while the camera eases in 1.1× over 0.8 s (power2.inOut); brackets snap in 0.12 s on the snare.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: density itself is the argument — this is what “watching everything” looks like — and the light, Swiss treatment keeps it trustworthy rather than sci-fi. Risk: at feed size dense panels are unreadable, so every beat must hold one panel hero-sized and blur the rest.

Adapt to your product: fill the sixteen panels with your own KPIs and let the hero panel be the one number your product protects; keep the brackets and scanline as the “our product is looking” device.

References: Edward Tufte — sparklines · Stripe Sessions 2025 — developer keynote
